claims.claim: Joseph Aspdin obtained the patent for Portland cement in 1824.
claims.episode_span: the same basic flow that Joseph Aspdin patented in 1824 and that large rotary kilns standardized by the early twentieth century
claims.supporting_quote: The cement was so named by Joseph Aspdin, who obtained a patent for it in 1824, because, once hardened, it resembled the fine, pale limestone known as Portland stone

claims.claim: Portland cement clinker is sintered in a kiln at a peak temperature of about 1,450 degrees Celsius.
claims.episode_span: fed into a kiln that reaches 1450 degrees Celsius
claims.supporting_quote: Typically, a peak temperature of 1400–1450 °C is required to complete the reaction.

claims.claim: A cement plant consumes on the order of 3-6 GJ of fuel per tonne of clinker produced, bracketing the digest's 3-4 GJ figure.
claims.episode_span: The energy input is dominated by the kiln, which needs on the order of three to four gigajoules per ton of clinker
claims.supporting_quote: A cement plant consumes 3 to 6 GJ of fuel per tonne of clinker produced, depending on the raw materials and the process used.

claims.claim: Decarbonation of limestone releases a fairly constant ~0.47-0.54 kg of process CO2 per kg of cement (typical ~0.50), matching the digest's ~0.5 t CO2 per ton figure.
claims.episode_span: adds another unavoidable mass loss—roughly 0.5 tons of CO2 per ton of clinker
claims.supporting_quote: Decarbonation of limestone Fairly constant: minimum around 0.47 kg (1.0 lb) CO 2 per kg of cement, maximum 0.54, typical value around 0.50 worldwide.

claims.claim: About 4 billion tonnes of cement are produced annually, accounting for roughly 8% of worldwide CO2 emissions.
claims.episode_span: the sheer volume of roughly four billion tons of cement produced annually. The prize is a material whose delivered cost moves measurably closer to the chemical and thermal floor while cutting the embedded emissions that currently make cement responsible for roughly eight percent of global CO2.
claims.supporting_quote: A Chatham House study from 2018 estimates that the 4 billion tonnes of cement produced annually account for 8% of worldwide CO 2 emissions.

claims.claim: In the kiln, calcium carbonate (limestone) decomposes to calcium oxide and CO2 before the calcium oxide combines with silica-bearing phases to form clinker.
claims.episode_span: Inside the kiln the limestone decomposes, releasing carbon dioxide, and the resulting calcium oxide combines with silica and alumina to form clinker nodules.
claims.supporting_quote: the remaining calcium carbonate decomposes to calcium oxide (CaO) and CO 2 . 1300 to 1450 °C – partial (20–30%) melting takes place, and belite reacts with calcium oxide to form alite

claims.claim: Joseph Aspdin was granted British Patent 5022 for 'An Improvement in the Mode of Producing an Artificial Stone' on 21 October 1824, coining the term Portland cement.
claims.episode_span: the same basic flow that Joseph Aspdin patented in 1824
claims.supporting_quote: on 21 October 1824 he was granted the British Patent BP 5022 entitled An Improvement in the Mode of Producing an Artificial Stone

claims.claim: In a cement kiln the raw material is heated to about 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit (about 1,480 C), making it partially molten, consistent with the digest's 1,450 C.
claims.episode_span: fed into a kiln that reaches 1450 degrees Celsius
claims.source_title: How Cement Is Made - Portland Cement Association
claims.supporting_quote: At the lower end of the kiln, a roaring flame heats the material to about 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit, making it partially molten.

claims.claim: Ground granulated blast-furnace slag replaces Portland cement one-to-one by weight at levels from 30% up to 85%, typically 40-50%.
claims.episode_span: partial substitution of clinker with supplementary materials such as ground granulated blast-furnace slag or calcined clay, which can replace 30 to 50 percent of the Portland component while maintaining strength
claims.supporting_quote: GGBS is used as a direct replacement for Portland cement, on a one-to-one basis by weight. Replacement levels for GGBS vary from 30% to up to 85%. Typically 40% to 50% is used in most instances.

claims.claim: Cement is the most energy-intensive of all US manufacturing industries, with a share of national energy use roughly ten times its share of gross output (EIA).
claims.episode_span: Each of those steps is capital-intensive and energy-intensive because the chemistry demands both heat and the right mineral phases.
claims.source_title: Energy-intensive cement industry - Today in Energy - U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
claims.supporting_quote: Although the cement industry used only one-quarter of one percent of total U.S. energy, it is the most energy-intensive of all manufacturing industries, with a share of national energy use roughly 10 times its share of the nation's gross output of goods and services
